photos.title: Ascending La Plata in March of 2021. We were post-holing up to our waist at times. {768x432}
Just after we gained the headwall of La Plata's standard route, the final false summit barely visible. {768x264}
The moon was still out just after first light.
First light seen along Humboldt's east ridge approach.
Photo of my summit sign on top of Humboldt Peak. Crestone Peak & Needle are visible in the background. {576x768}
A screenshot of my peak checklist on 14ers.com. See how the Snowflake appears opposite the standard mark of completion. {375x291}
Can you see why the line on the right might be riskier? {768x341}
Looking north to Snowmass and Capitol Peaks from between the Maroon Bells.
Near the top of the first gully descending North Maroon with Pyramid Peak in view.
Bushwhacking through the a wildflower-filled field to return to the main Herman Gulch trail. {768x545}
Standing on Citadel’s true summit, looking over to Pettingell. {768x524}
Standing on the initial false summit of The Citadel, looking over to the real summit block. {768x514}
Blue rope and an anchor is visible closer to the bottom of this photo, the chute I've just climbed to the right. Grays and Torreys on the horizon. {576x768}
Looking up the chute I chose to climb, visible as a crack on the far right. {576x768}
Hugging Maroon’s southwest shoulder after ascending the first chimney.
You get your first look at Maroon’s summit after topping out on the “2,800 feet of suck”. {768x522}
Comparing options for the third spire, North Maroon’s summit visible beyond this set of obstacles. {768x408}
Finally reaching grass at the end of a seemingly never-ending scree slope near the end of our descent of North Maroon, a storm visibly brewing.
Jason looking up at the remaining route to North Maroon from a gap crossing past the third spire.
This robot-shaped guardian lets you know you're near a turning point. {768x534}
A closer look at a well-marked section of Maroon Peak’s southwest ridge trail.
Standing on North Maroon’s summit with Maroon Peak and the route we just traversed in the background. {768x528}
Dropping off of Maroon Peak, beginning the Bells Traverse. {768x510}
Me, nearing the top of those 2,800 Feet. Photo by my climbing partner Luis. {768x512}
Looking for a line on the second spire.
Watching the sun set over Gunnison Reservoir in Curecanti Recreation Area. {768x498}
Alpenglow seen against Mount Antero as I left the parking lot.
Looking over to the 13,630' peak that shares a saddle with Shavano, "Esprit Point". {768x330}
A downed tree with evidence of where hikers prior had to manuever over it. {547x768}
Some deer watching me run out of the wilderness. {798x496}
My glissade tracks, from up close and far away. {768x590}
A closer look at that punchcrust and what my snowshoes were doing to it. {576x768}
The beginning of sunrise, seen from the parking lot. {798x498}
Standard trail visible to the left. {768x553}
Rock hopping before I commit to my crampons. {576x768}
Looking back down to the base of the Angel after gaining some elevation. {576x768}
Dropping off of the summit of Shavano. {768x552}
Looking back at the last bit of Maroon's descent from across the Bell Cord. Zoom in to see our climbing partner Jason y down the 20 foot wall. {557x768}
Looking back at the couloir just as storm clouds roll in. {798x518}
On the summit of Mount Shavano, looking at the traverse over to Tabeguache Peak. {768x289}
Some of my less exciting glissade tracks off of the summit block.
My first view of the Angel. {768x503}
This where I gave up on my snowshoes, stashing them somewhere underneath a tree to the left of this image. {541x768}
